title: Unitary synthesis from a Boolean oracle
description: One quantum oracle circuit, generated in polynomial time from n alone, with polynomially many qubits, gates H, T, T*, CNOT and oracle calls, approximates every n-qubit unitary within diamond-norm distance 1/2 once a suitable Boolean oracle is chosen. The proof: programmable slots; a diagonal block of small norm from random signs and Walsh-Hadamard transforms; the transfer function of the block matrix and two nearly isometric field maps with few nonzero Fourier coefficients per row; amplitude amplification and a recursion that calls the smaller circuit once per level; compilation of every slot into words in H, T, T* read from one oracle, with the phases kept. The course is an exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026).

units.title: Oracle circuits and the synthesis theorem
Fourier fields for a smaller unitary

prerequisites: core course Real Analysis II (Lebl, Basic Analysis II): the inverse function theorem (Theorem 8.5.1); compactness and continuity in finite dimensions
linear algebra over the complex numbers: inner products, operator norms, unitary and Hermitian matrices, tensor products
probability on finite sets and Gaussian integrals: independence, expectation, Markov's and Jensen's inequalities, Fubini's theorem, integration by parts
